thread:
Maya: FYI — AcmePay filed a ticket: lots of 403s after we onboarded their SSO service account. They say embeddings and rerank work but generation calls are failing. ticket #98765
Alex: Got the ticket link, thanks. Do we have an example request/response from them?
Maya: Pasted below (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "open-redwood-1",
  "input": "Hello"
}

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": {
    "message": "insufficient_scope: missing scope: generation",
    "code": 403
  }
}
```
Maya: They also included logs showing embeddings requests returning 200.
Jamal: That error string is specific — token lacks the generation scope. Did the SSO provisioning job map groups to scopes correctly?
Lina: I recall the new SSO flow creates a service key with scopes derived from the app role. If the role is "read_embeddings,rerank" only it would explain the behaviour.
cs-bot: Ticket #98765 updated by Maya: assigned to Eng-CS for repro. :eyes:
Alex: I can repro locally by creating a token with embeddings+rerank only. Quick repro steps:
```bash
# create token with limited scopes (simulated)
export TEST_KEY=sk-test-limited
# call generate
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-redwood-1","input":"hi"}' | jq
# response shows 403 + missing scope
```
Alex: Confirms it's a scopes mismatch.
Maya: Customer says the service key was created via SSO provisioning flow in their IdP, they didn't set scopes manually.
Jamal: Can we check the provisioning lambda mapping? ops-bot, any recent deploys to the provisioner?
ops-bot: Deploy note: provisioner v2.3.1 rolled 2026-02-12 03:12 UTC — mapping change included.
Lina: On v2.3.1 we introduced an override that strips "generate" from service keys unless the enterprise flag is set. It was to prevent token creep but maybe too aggressive.
Maya: That would explain why existing tokens look fine but newly provisioned SSO keys are missing generation. AcmePay is new onboarding.
Alex: Short-term fix: we can re-issue the service key for them with explicit scopes including "generation:invoke" (or equivalent config). Long-term: change provisioner default or add tenant allowlist.
Maya: Customer asked for a fix today — can we re-provision and test with them?
Jamal: I'm pushing a change to re-enable generation for the enterprise org flag. Patch: add back default generation scope for orgs that passed SSO onboarding checks.
Lina: Also adding audit log entry so we can trace which provisioner version created a given key.
Alex: For the immediate repro verification, I patched my local provisioning mapping and re-created a token; generation succeeds.
Maya: I'll coordinate with AcmePay CS rep and ask them to try a replaced key. Holding message to them now.
cs-bot: Customer notified: new key pending.
Maya: Customer tested the replacement key — they report generate now returns 200. :tada: Embeddings/rerank still fine.
Maya: Ticket update to customer: "We found an overly-restrictive default in our SSO provisioning service that omitted generation scope for some newly-created service keys. We've re-provisioned your key and verified generation calls succeed. We're rolling out a fix to the provisioner and will add audit logging. Sorry for the disruption."
Alex: Follow-ups: (1) Add a quick E2E test in CS onboarding that validates generate+embeddings+rerank on any newly-created service key. (2) Rollback the override in provisioner v2.3.2 with a migration to backfill keys for orgs created since 2026-02-12.
Jamal: I'll open the PR for v2.3.2 now and tag eng-oncall for a canary.
Lina: I'll add a monitoring alert to detect spikes of "insufficient_scope: missing scope: generation" errors in the next 24h.
Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll mark the ticket as pending-customer-ack then resolved once they confirm in 24h.
ops-bot: CI: provisioning-e2e passed in canary -> 3/3 workers.
Alex: Nice work. Closing loop in the runbook: add a note under "SSO provisioning" about the scope mapping.
Maya: Closing note: customer happy, will follow up if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
